html:
Dutch painter, born in 1853, who did his best known work in the south of France. He sold almost nothing in his life and is now one of the most famous artists in the world.

He came to art late. His early pictures, such as The Potato Eaters, are dark and show peasant life. In Paris from 1886 he met the Impressionists and his colours turned bright.

In 1888 he moved to Arles in Provence, where he painted the Sunflowers, orchards and night scenes in thick, bold strokes. Paul Gauguin joined him, but they quarrelled, and in a breakdown Van Gogh cut off part of his own ear. He then spent a year in an asylum at Saint-Rémy, where he painted The Starry Night (1889).

He made about 2,100 works, most in his last two years. He shot himself and died in 1890 at Auvers-sur-Oise, aged 37. His brother Theo, who supported him all his life, died months later. He is a founder of Post-Impressionism.
sum: Dutch painter, born in 1853, who did his best known work in the south of France. He sold almost nothing in his life and is now one of the most famous artists in the world.
